text: The constructor replaces the integer carrier by N⊆L and retains the ambient rational form. The IsLattice instance supplies finite generation and full rational span; integrality follows from the inclusion. This is the full sublattice case of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), without pretending an arbitrary submodule spans V. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L222) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L228) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L298) passes.
The new carrier is precisely N.
The ambient form is unchanged.
When full, the rationalized restriction comparison is the extension of the inclusion.

The finite free module embeds by m↦1⊗m into ℚ⊗M. Its integer image is full there, and the form extends by [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139), taking the original integer values on unit tensors. Thus this is the embedded realization of the abstract integral form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), allowing degeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L135) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L174) passes.
The carrier is the actual image of the unit-tensor map.
Restricting the extended form recovers B exactly.

Full restriction keeps V and its rational bilinear form, so nondegeneracy is literally the same property. Only the integral carrier changes. This agrees with the full sublattice construction in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); no analogous claim is made for arbitrary lower-rank restrictions. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L228) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L222) passes.
The rational form is unchanged.
Only the full integer submodule is replaced.

Every vector in N belongs to L, and the retained form has the same self-pairing on it. Evenness on all of L therefore restricts to N, exactly the definition in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). This is a one-way inheritance statement and does not assert the converse. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L228) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L222) passes.
The pairing is unchanged on the smaller carrier.
The new carrier is the supplied submodule N.

The full-restriction constructor stores exactly L.form on the original rational space. Thus the equation specifies which ambient form the new carrier inherits, as required for a sublattice in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); it is not a new form on a different ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L222) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L298) passes.
The separately changed datum is the carrier N.
The comparison with restriction in its own rationalization uses the actual inclusion.

Negation scales the bilinear form by−1 and keeps the carrier. Applying it twice multiplies the form by1, so this is an involution on integral lattices. It is precisely the negative form in the scaling convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), not negation of the carrier set. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L273) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L277) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L127) passes.
Negation fixes the integral carrier.
It negates the rational pairing.
The rank-one family gives the expected sign reversal.

The radical of−B equals the radical of B: multiplying every pairing by−1 does not change whether it vanishes. Hence a nondegenerate lattice remains nondegenerate after the form negation of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), regardless of definiteness. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L350) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L364) passes.
The underlying equivalence proves preservation and reflection.
The full radical is unchanged.

An integer self-pairing is divisible by2 exactly when its negative is. Since form negation fixes the carrier, the displayed equivalence is precisely preservation of the parity definition in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), even for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L289) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L127) passes.
The restricted pairing is negated exactly.
The rank-one model realizes parameter sign reversal.

The carrier is the image of m↦1⊗m. Freeness makes this map injective over ℤ→ℚ, and its image gives surjectivity onto the carrier, yielding the specified integral equivalence. Together with [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139), this realizes the abstract lattice of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) without choosing new vector coordinates. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L158) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L165) passes.
The equivalence sends m to1⊗m.
Its inverse recovers m from that unit tensor.

Base change evaluates on 1⊗x and1⊗y to the rational cast of B(x,y) by [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139). The restricted integral pairing has that same cast, and injectivity of ℤ→ℚ gives the asserted integer equality. No factor of two or nondegeneracy premise appears. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L158) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L206) passes.
The carrier vectors are exactly the specified unit tensors.
The canonical rationalization round trip is identity.

The constructor stores the chosen full submodule N as its carrier, so the equality is literal. In particular it does not replace N by its saturation or rational span. The ambient-span hypothesis is supplied separately, as required for the full sublattice model of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Restriction.lean#L228) passes.
The original ambient rational form is retained.

Integer multiplication acts by scaling the form and retaining the carrier. Scaling by1 changes nothing, and scaling by n then m multiplies the pairing by mn. These are exactly the two MulAction laws for the lattice scaling operation in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), including scalar0. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L114) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L109) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L160) passes.
The rational pairing is multiplied by the integer cast.
The integer carrier remains fixed.
The determinant scales by n to the unchanged rank.

Negation is scaling the form by−1, and scaling leaves the carrier fixed by definition. This equation therefore expresses the form-negation convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); it makes no identification of distinct rational forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L277) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L283) passes.
The form itself changes sign.
The unchanged carrier retains its rank.

Scaling by−1 multiplies the rational pairing by−1, which is its additive negative. This is the exact form-negation operation from [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); carrier preservation is separate from the sign change of self-pairings. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L289) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L384) passes.
The integer restriction changes sign on every pair.
Positive and negative signature indices are exchanged.

For every x, the functional−B(x,·) vanishes exactly when B(x,·) vanishes. Their radicals coincide, so nondegeneracy is equivalent in both directions for the negative form of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Degenerate and zero-dimensional cases are included. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L364) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L127) passes.
The source proves equality of the radicals themselves.
The rank-one model verifies the form-sign convention.

The equivalence into the carrier is the unit-tensor map followed by the equality identifying its image with that carrier. Forgetting the subtype therefore yields exactly1⊗x. This is the vector realization used by [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139), independent of the chosen construction basis. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L165) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L174) passes.
The inverse recovers the original vector.
The realized vectors retain their original integral pairings.

The integer span of the base-changed basis is exactly the range of m↦1⊗m. Thus the carrier realizes the original integral module, rather than the entire rational tensor space. This is the embedded form of the finite-free lattice in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), compatible with [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L141) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L158) passes.
Membership means being a unit pure tensor.
The canonical carrier equivalence uses that exact map.

The ambient form is the rational scalar extension of B. In particular its value on q⊗x and r⊗y is qr times the cast of B(x,y), by [Mathlib’s bilinear base-change formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/TensorProduct.lean#L139). The construction neither halves the pairing nor assumes it is nondegenerate. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L174) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Rationalization.lean#L68) passes.
Unit tensors recover the original integer form.
Rationalizing the integral restriction returns the ambient form.

This definitional equality says precisely that negating a lattice means scaling its form by the integer−1. It exposes the scaling convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); it does not define a new carrier or claim an isometry to the original form. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L277) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L273) passes.
The rational form is the negative of the original.
The integer carrier is unchanged.

For n≠0, multiplication by its rational cast is injective. Thus nB(x,y)=0 for all y exactly when B(x,y)=0 for all y, giving equality of radical conditions. This is the nonzero-scaling behavior of the form in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3); zero scaling is explicitly excluded. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L181) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L212) passes.
The same hypothesis gives equality of radicals.
The zero rank-one form supplies the degeneracy boundary.

The operation keeps L.carrier and replaces B by nB. An integer multiple of each integral pairing is integral, so the result is an integral lattice with the same full carrier. This is exactly the form twist L(n) in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), distinct from dilating lattice vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L109) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L125) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L160) passes.
The carrier is fixed, including when n=0.
The integral pairing is multiplied by n.
The signed determinant scales by n to the lattice rank.

The integer action was defined to multiply the rational form by the canonical cast of n. Hence this equation exposes exactly the form twist in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3), with the correct scalar ring. It holds for zero and negative scalars as well. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L125) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Scaling.lean#L142) passes.
The restricted integer pairing scales by the same integer.
Every integral Gram entry scales by n.

Evaluating universal conjugation at the constant point g in its first tensor factor gives the pullback of x↦gxg⁻¹ from [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). Published [all-value-point](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L68) and [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L83) controls pass. The construction works over commutative semirings; convolution inversion uses the antipode, without additive subtraction or a field hypothesis.
Precomposition gives g_A x g_A⁻¹ over every commutative value semiring.
Identity convolution point induces the identity coordinate map.

The coordinate map, viewed as an H-valued point, is g_H·id_H·g_H⁻¹, exactly the universal-point specialization of [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The published [arbitrary-value evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L68) passes. Multiplication is convolution of algebra maps, not pointwise multiplication of functions; g is transported along the base algebra map before forming this product.
Precomposition gives g_A x g_A⁻¹ over every commutative value semiring.

Conjugation by the convolution identity fixes the universal point, so its coordinate pullback is AlgHom.id, as required by [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The published [Hopf-ideal identity control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Conjugation.lean#L94) passes over rings. The coordinate identity itself holds already over commutative semirings, with the counit giving the identity point and no finite-type assumption.
The induced operation fixes every closed-subgroup ideal at the identity point.

Since conjugation by gh is conjugation by h followed by g, coordinate pullback composes as c_h♯∘c_g♯, matching [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The published [closed-subgroup action control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Conjugation.lean#L101) passes. The displayed reversal is essential for noncommuting points; Lean requires neither cocommutativity nor commutativity of the represented point group.
Coordinate composition gives the ordinary left action on closed-subgroup ideals.

Inner conjugation preserves the group law and identity and has inverse conjugation by g⁻¹, as in [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). Source verifies counit and comultiplication compatibility and constructs the inverse. Published [point-formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L166) and [surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L160) controls pass. BialgEquiv is the appropriate Hopf-coordinate automorphism, also over commutative semirings.
Underlying bialgebra equivalence induces the correct pointwise inner automorphism.
The coordinate bialgebra automorphism is actually surjective.

Forgetting the bialgebra-equivalence structure recovers exactly the conjugation pullback constructed from [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The published [point-formula control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/PointConjugation.lean#L166) passes. The bijective-equivalence wrapper preserves the forward algebra map; this equality fixes its orientation and prevents confusing the map with the inverse conjugation pullback.
Underlying bialgebra equivalence induces the correct pointwise inner automorphism.

The underlying map of the constructed conjugation equivalence is surjective, since conjugation by g⁻¹ supplies its inverse as in [Milne, inner automorphisms](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=43). The published [Hopf-ideal inverse-image control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Conjugation.lean#L74) passes. This is surjectivity of this particular coordinate automorphism, not a claim that arbitrary Hopf morphisms induce surjections on rational points.
The surjective coordinate automorphism supports the advertised Hopf-ideal inverse image.

Integer numeral powers agree with the corresponding natural numeral powers. The two exponents have different types despite similar rendered notation. For a>0, the inequality a⁻¹≤b is equivalent to 1≤b·a. The positive multiplier is applied on the right, matching MulPosReflectLT. This remains valid without commutativity; replacing b·a by a·b would use different compatibility assumptions. For c>0, c⁻¹·b≤a is equivalent to b≤c·a. Multiplication by c occurs on the left and preserves the inequality. The source correctly needs PosMulReflectLT and makes no commutativity assumption. For c>0, a≤c⁻¹·b is equivalent to c·a≤b. The left multiplication order is essential in a noncommutative group. A partial order and the stated left multiplication compatibility suffice; total order is unnecessary. For b≠0, a=b⁻¹·c is equivalent to b·a=c. This is left cancellation in a group with zero, with the multiplication order preserved. No commutativity or order hypothesis is needed. In a group with a left-translation-invariant strict relation, 1<a⁻¹ is equivalent to a<1. Multiplying on the left by a gives the equivalence. The theorem assumes only LT and MulLeftStrictMono, not a full preorder or linear order. Every integer power of a positive element is positive, including negative exponents. The proof uses positivity of natural powers and of inverses. ZeroLEOneClass handles exponent zero, and the source only requires a partial order with the stated left multiplication compatibility. Every integer power of a nonnegative element is nonnegative. The zero base is allowed: its exponent-zero value is one, and its other integer powers are zero. Negative exponents use the total inverse convention, which agrees with ordinary inverses on positive elements.
